competitorWins: NASA Worldview is an extraordinary free research tool: over 1,000 full-resolution satellite layers, most updated within 3 hours of observation, some spanning nearly 30 years, geostationary imagery in 10-minute increments, event pins for cyclones, wildfires and eruptions, custom time-lapse animations, layer transparency and comparison tools — open source, backed by NASA's EOSDIS, with the underlying data downloadable. For environmental science and disaster analysis, its scientific layer library is unmatched for free.
description: NASA Worldview (NASA's EOSDIS) is a free, open-source interactive browser for near real-time satellite imagery: 1,000+ global layers updated within ~3 hours of observation, event tracking pins, time-lapse animations and layer comparisons — all in a web browser with no signup. It is science-first, not an everyday viewer. WorldEye is complementary for the general audience: satellite imagery on a free, signup-free 3D globe that also carries live flights, ships, ~76,000 cameras, weather, quakes and wildfires in one beautiful view.
